newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian police trade gunfire during protest march.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian police trade gunfire during protest march.

text.p: Brazilian police traded shots with other police in the northeastern city of Fortaleza on Tuesday after the authorities tried to break up a protest march by officers demanding better pay, officials said.
An official at military police headquarters in Fortaleza, capital of the state of Ceara, said the military police commander had been hit and was in hospital.
"People starting firing and the commander was hit. But he is not in danger," the official said.
Local news agencies reported that a military police squad had tried to break up a demonstration by civil police officers when both sides started firing widely.
The army was put on alert to deal with any new flare-up.
Like thousands of their colleagues around the country, police in Ceara are seeking better pay and conditions.
On Monday, police representatives said most had ended their month-long strike and would go back to work.
The police strike, which has affected more than a dozen of Brazil's 27 states, has exposed serious fault lines in the country's creaking public security apparatus.
Almost two weeks ago, striking police traded shots with soldiers guarding the legislative assembly in Maceio, capital of Alagoas state.
And last month, one officer died after a clash between striking civil police and military police in Belo Horizonte, capital of Minas Gerais state.
